summary: Kentucky and Indiana are both in VA CCN Region 2, so VA community care claims go to Optum (VA CCN region page). Do they have to answer? For VA, yes, by statute: 38 U.S.C. 1703D(a) requires payment of a clean claim within 30 days of receipt (electronic) or 45 days (paper), a written denial with the reason and the missing information within the same periods, and a decision within 30 days after requested information arrives. VA's own Financial Policy (Vol. VIII ch. 02, 2024) applies this to every Veterans Community Care contract, including CCN. A claim that misses these clocks is 'overdue' by statute and must be counted in VA's annual report to Congress by facility and VISN. What happens if they do not: less than the owner hopes. Interest is discretionary ('may'), at the Treasury Prompt Payment rate (4.75% for July-December 2026). VA promised rules on interest and timeframes in 2019 and none were found through November 2026. VA wrote in the Federal Register in 2024 that 'if VA fails to pay a valid, submitted claim, it owes interest for late payment', but Optum's November 2026 manual is silent on interest, so interest on CCN claims is a documented request, not a confirmed entitlement. 1703D has no fine and no private right of action. Optum's own written commitments add pressure points: 98% of clean claims in 30 days; non-clean claims returned with reasons within 30 days; reconsiderations within 90 days of denial, many claims per letter; underpayment inquiries within 12 months; escalation if no answer in 45 days; recoupment disputes answered in about 30 business days, with offset only after day 61. Rules that cut against the practice: 180-day timely filing that Optum says it is 'contractually prohibited' from waiving except for claims first misdirected to VA or another TPA; Veterans are held harmless and other insurance may not be billed, so every CCN dollar must come from Optum; CPT codes outside the referral's episode of care (SEOC) are denied unless VA approves a Request for Services. Escalation to VA for CCN claims: VA says CCN disputes follow 'the terms of your contract' (the practice's Optum/UnitedHealthcare agreement, not public); no separate VA appeal of a CCN claim was found. A formal VA dispute process with a VA decision deadline and court review exists only for Veterans Care Agreements (38 CFR 17.4135). CHAMPVA (VA-paid, secondary to Medicare) has 1-year filing and 1-year Higher-Level Review, and VA lists it as exempt from the Prompt Payment Act. TRICARE likely applies: Humana Military's East Region covers Kentucky and Indiana, and TRICARE For Life (WPS) wraps Medicare for military retirees, so missed TFL crossovers are a 'secondary never billed' category. 10 U.S.C. 1095c requires 95% of clean claims processed in 30 days and 100% in 100 days; interest is discretionary (the Operations Manual could not be checked); TRICARE may not demand more claim information than Medicare. Filing is 1 year from service (32 CFR 199.7(d)). Most payment disputes, including network contract-rate underpayments, go to Humana Military administrative/allowable charge review within 90 days of the remittance. Formal appeals are only for medical-necessity/coverage denials, and network providers need the patient's signed appointment. Contractors 'normally' decide reconsiderations within 60 days, and even tiny amounts cannot be rejected at reconsideration. Leverage, honestly: the strongest truthful levers are the statutory clocks, the 'overdue' label with Congressional reporting, the payer's own written commitments and the offset protections in 1703D(e). Both are federal programs: 1703D(c) applies the False Claims Act to provider claims, so every automated letter must be factually exact and must not claim entitlements the text does not give.

rules.citation: 38 U.S.C. 1703D(a)(1), with (a)(4) (invoice-basis only), (g)(1) (VA may process through its CCN contractor) and (i)(2)-(3) (clean claim definitions)
rules.quote: the Secretary shall pay for hospital care, medical services, or extended care services furnished by health care entities or providers under this chapter within 45 calendar days upon receipt of a clean paper claim or 30 calendar days upon receipt of a clean electronic claim.
rules.applies_to: VA as payer for community care under 38 U.S.C. chapter 17 furnished by any non-Department provider: VA CCN claims that Optum pays for VA in CCN Region 2 (Kentucky and Indiana, per VA's CCN page), Veterans Care Agreements and other VA-paid authorized care. VA's own Financial Policy (Vol. VIII ch. 02 sec. 020509) applies 1703D to 'any contracts and agreements within the Veterans Community Care Program', and VA's CCN dental-provider fact sheet IB-10-1379 (updated Jan. 24, 2022) lists 'Prompt payment within 30 days of receipt of clean claims, including resubmissions' as a CCN benefit. Invoice-basis payments only, not capitation. Not insurance law, so fully-insured vs self-funded and state prompt-pay distinctions do not arise. Official text current through Pub. L. 119-142 (Nov. 10, 2026); last amended 2018.
rules.requires: Pay a clean claim within 30 calendar days of receipt if electronic, 45 if paper. A clean claim 'contains substantially all of the required data elements necessary for accurate adjudication, without obtaining additional information from the entity or provider' (1703D(i)(2)-(3)).
rules.deadline: 30 calendar days from receipt of a clean electronic claim; 45 calendar days from receipt of a clean paper claim.
rules.consequence: The claim becomes 'overdue' under 1703D(d)(1) (see VA-03 for interest and VA-07 for the report to Congress). The statute names no automatic penalty, no fine and no private right of action.
rules.provider_use: For every VA CCN claim whose 277CA acceptance date is more than 30 days old with no payment, no denial and no pend notice, send a batched letter citing 1703D(a)(1) and (d)(1), listing each claim's receipt date and days elapsed, and demanding payment or a written denial with reasons. Optum accepts many claims in one letter (VA-11).

rules.quote: If a claim is denied, the Secretary shall, within 45 calendar days of denial for a paper claim and 30 calendar days of denial for an electronic claim, notify the health care entity or provider of the reason for denying the claim and what, if any, additional information is required to process the claim.
rules.applies_to: Same as VA-01 (VA CCN through Optum, VCAs, VA-paid authorized care).
rules.requires: A written denial that states the reason and what additional information is needed. Then (a)(3): 'Upon the receipt of the additional information, the Secretary shall ensure that the claim is paid, denied, or otherwise adjudicated within 30 calendar days from the receipt of the requested information.'
rules.deadline: Denial notice within 30 days (electronic) or 45 days (paper) of the denial; final adjudication within 30 calendar days after the requested information is received.
rules.consequence: A claim not denied with notice, pended with notice or paid within these periods is 'overdue' under 1703D(d)(1). No automatic penalty.
rules.provider_use: When a denial gives no reason or no list of what is missing, demand the statutory notice. After sending requested records, start a 30-day clock; on day 31 send an overdue notice citing 1703D(a)(3). Keep fax confirmations and Optum PRA dates as proof.

rules.citation: 38 U.S.C. 1703D(d)(1)-(2); 31 U.S.C. 3902(a)-(b); Treasury Prompt Payment interest rate table
rules.quote: If a claim is overdue under this subsection, the Secretary may, under the requirements established by subsection (a) and consistent with the provisions of chapter 39 of title 31 (commonly referred to as the “Prompt Payment Act”), require that interest be paid on clean claims.
rules.applies_to: Overdue clean claims under VA community care (CCN, VCAs, VA-paid authorized care). Whether Optum pays interest on CCN claims is not confirmed: Optum's November 2026 manual is silent on interest.
rules.requires: Nothing mandatory: VA 'may' require interest. If paid, the rate is the Treasury Prompt Payment rate (1703D(d)(2)(B)): 4.75% for July 1 - December 31, 2026 (91 FR 42594); 4.125% for January 1 - June 30, 2026 (91 FR 5035); 4.625% for both halves of 2025. Under 31 U.S.C. 3902(b) interest runs from the day after the due date to the payment date.
rules.deadline: Interest would start the day after the 30-day (electronic) or 45-day (paper) due date.
rules.consequence: Discretionary only. In 2019 VA promised rulemaking on 'interest on overdue claims' (84 FR 26301); no such rule was found in the Federal Register through November 2026, so there is no regulation that makes interest automatic.
rules.provider_use: Request interest (do not call it an entitlement) on each overdue clean claim, with the amount computed per claim at the Treasury rate, citing 1703D(d)(2), VA Financial Policy sec. 020509 (VA-06) and VA's own statement at 89 FR 67864 (VA-05). Expect refusals; the value is pressure plus a record that Congress-reportable overdue claims exist.

rules.quote: Deductions may not be made under this subsection unless the Secretary has made reasonable efforts to notify a health care entity or provider of the right to dispute the existence or amount of such indebtedness and the right to request a compromise of such indebtedness.
rules.applies_to: VA overpayment deductions from payments due under chapter 17. Whether Optum's own CCN recoupments count as deductions 'under this subsection' is not confirmed (Optum recovers 'pursuant to VA CCN requirements').
rules.requires: Before offsetting: notice of the right to dispute and the right to request a compromise. (e)(3): 'The Secretary shall make a determination with respect to any such dispute or request prior to deducting any overpayment unless the time required to make such a determination before making any deductions would jeopardize the Secretary's ability to recover the full amount of such indebtedness.'
rules.deadline: None fixed in the statute; the dispute must be decided before the deduction.
rules.consequence: An offset taken without that notice, or before a pending dispute is decided, is contrary to the statute; the remedy is a written dispute demanding reversal.
rules.provider_use: Dispute every VA or Optum recoupment in writing before the offset date (Optum offsets at day 61, see VA-16), cite 1703D(e)(2)-(3), request a compromise where the debt is real, and demand no offset until the dispute is decided.

rules.citation: 89 FR 67863-67865 (Aug. 22, 2024), VA notification 'Processing Certain Claims for Payment for Transportation, Care, and Services', at 67864
rules.quote: In general, if VA fails to pay a valid, submitted claim, it owes interest for late payment.
rules.applies_to: Written about claims submitted directly to VA (payer IDs 12115, 12116, and family-member IDs 84146, 84147) during the Change Healthcare outage; it states VA's general position. Not written about Optum-paid CCN claims.
rules.requires: VA states that 'if VA fails to pay claims submitted now, it will be liable for interest payments under relevant provisions of law.' The same notice reads 1703D(b)'s 180-day filing rule as excused by force majeure and impossibility for that outage, and quotes Congress: 'VA's ability to timely and accurately process payments to community providers is critical to the [Community Care] Program's success'.
rules.deadline: The outage relief itself required claims received by Oct. 31, 2024 (expired).
rules.consequence: Interpretive guidance, not a penalty provision.
rules.provider_use: Quote it when asking VA for interest on directly-paid claims (VCA, unauthorized emergency) and as persuasive authority in CCN interest requests. When a filing miss was caused by an event outside the practice's control, cite its force majeure reasoning (no guarantee it will be extended to other events).

rules.citation: VA Financial Policy, Volume VIII, Chapter 02 'Invoice Review and Certification', secs. 020507 and 020509 (approved June 14, 2024)
rules.quote: In accordance with 38 U.S.C. § 1703D, VA may pay an interest penalty to any Veteran Community Care Program entity or provider for payments not made by the required due date.
rules.applies_to: VA payments under the Veterans Community Care Program. Sec. 020507 lists 'Community Care Network (CCN); and Veterans Care Agreements' among 'VA payments subject to PPA', yet the same section lists 'Payments for community care falling under 38 U.S.C. § 1703D' and CHAMPVA among PPA exemptions. The policy is internally inconsistent on CCN.
rules.requires: Sec. 020509: 'VA will follow prompt payment standards as established in 38 U.S.C. § 1703D for any contracts and agreements within the Veterans Community Care Program' (45/30 days to pay; denial notice in 45/30 days; payment within 30 days after requested information). 'A clean claim functions as an invoice for the Veterans Community Care Program.'
rules.deadline: Same as VA-01 and VA-02.
rules.consequence: Internal agency policy, not a regulation; interest stays discretionary.
rules.provider_use: Cite it when anyone argues 1703D does not reach CCN claims, and quote sec. 020507's listing of CCN under PPA-subject payments when requesting interest. Do not assert a guaranteed right to Prompt Payment Act interest or the PPA additional penalty for CCN claims.

rules.quote: Not less frequently than annually, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on payment of overdue claims under this subsection, disaggregated by paper and electronic claims
rules.applies_to: VA (duty to report). Covers overdue claims under 1703D(d).
rules.requires: Annual report giving the amount paid on overdue claims and the interest paid, plus 'The number of such overdue claims and the average number of days late each claim was paid, disaggregated by facility of the Department and Veterans Integrated Service Network region.'
rules.deadline: At least annually.
rules.consequence: Late payments become visible to Congress by VA facility and VISN.
rules.provider_use: A truthful, non-threatening lever: state that the listed claims are overdue claims under 1703D(d), which VA counts in its annual report to Congress. For persistent non-payment, a congressional caseworker inquiry is a practical channel (a civic option, not a legal right created by this statute).

rules.citation: 38 U.S.C. 1703D(f)(1)-(3); VA request for information, 84 FR 32670 (July 9, 2019)
rules.quote: If the Secretary modifies the information and documentation included in the list under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall notify all health care entities and providers described in paragraph (1) not later than 30 days before such modifications take effect.
rules.applies_to: VA community care programs under chapter 17, including CCN.
rules.requires: (f)(1): VA 'shall provide to all health care entities and providers participating in a program ... a list of information and documentation that is required to establish a clean claim under this section', and must give 30 days' notice before changing it.
rules.deadline: 30 days' advance notice of any change to the clean-claim list.
rules.consequence: A denial for an element not on the published list, or for a new requirement imposed without 30 days' notice, is open to challenge.
rules.provider_use: When a claim is denied as incomplete, ask Optum or VA to identify where the element appears on the 1703D(f) clean-claim list and when providers were notified. I did not find the final published list (VA sought comments in 2019); treat its existence as an open question.

rules.citation: 38 U.S.C. 1703D(b); Optum VA CCN Provider Manual (Nov. 2026) 'Timely Filing', p. 44; Optum Medical Service Model and Claims Guide (Nov. 2026), pp. 2-3
rules.quote: Claims must be submitted within one hundred-eighty (180) calendar days from the date of service for outpatient care or the date of discharge for inpatient care.
rules.applies_to: The practice (provider duty) on every VA CCN claim; 1703D(b) applies the same 180 days to chapter 17 claims generally.
rules.requires: File within 180 days of the date of service. Exceptions in the manual: a claim first sent in error to VA or another VA TPA may go to Optum within 180 days of that denial with proof (VA EOP, TPA remittance or 277 rejection); if Optum receives the referral after the date of service, 180 days from the date Optum received the referral (the claims guide says from the date VA issues the referral).
rules.deadline: 180 calendar days from the date of service.
rules.consequence: Late claims are denied; the claims guide says 'Optum is contractually prohibited from waiving timely filing for anything outside of the scenario listed above'; and the Veteran cannot be billed (VA-14), so the money is lost.
rules.provider_use: Treat day 180 as a hard stop for unanswered or rejected CCN claims: resubmit with proof well before it. For misdirected claims, keep the VA/TPA denial and resubmit within 180 days of it. Use the earlier of the two referral-date readings.

rules.citation: Optum VA CCN Provider Manual (Nov. 2026), 'Claims Processing Timelines', p. 45
rules.quote: Optum is committed to processing 98% of all clean claims within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of the clean claim.
rules.applies_to: Optum-processed VA CCN claims (Regions 1-3; Kentucky and Indiana are Region 2).
rules.requires: Also: 'Claims that do not meet the definition of a clean claim will be returned to the provider with an explanation of deficiencies within thirty (30) calendar days of being received' and 'All claims submitted will be acknowledged either with a payment, a provider remittance advice or returned with a specific request for additional information.' Optum's clean claim = all data elements needed 'to be accepted by the clearinghouse and/or the payer's adjudication system'.
rules.deadline: 30 calendar days from receipt (payment for clean claims; deficiency letter for non-clean claims).
rules.consequence: None stated (a published performance commitment).
rules.provider_use: Pair with VA-01: the statute requires every clean claim to be paid in 30 days, not 98% of them. A claim with no payment, no remittance and no deficiency letter after 30 days misses both Optum's written commitment and the statute.

rules.citation: Optum VA CCN Provider Manual (Nov. 2026), 'Claim Reconsiderations', p. 48; Optum Medical Service Model and Claims Guide (Nov. 2026), pp. 2-3
rules.quote: When a claim is denied partially or in whole, a reconsideration request must be filed within ninety (90) calendar days from the date of denial
rules.applies_to: Denied or partly denied Optum VA CCN claims.
rules.requires: Written request with claim number, date of service, Veteran name, reason and justification. 'Providers can request reconsiderations of multiple claims in a single letter.' Send to the address or fax on the remittance advice, otherwise fax 1-877-666-6597, Region 2 email faxAG2@optumserve.com, or VA Community Care Network Appeals and Grievance Team MS-21, 3237 Airport Road, La Crosse, WI 54603. Optum sets no written decision deadline; the claims guide says: 'If you haven't received a response within forty-five (45) calendar days from your original submission, you may escalate your inquiry further by calling our Provider Services support team'.
rules.deadline: 90 calendar days from the date of denial (the claims guide counts from the date on the PRA; use the earlier). Escalation point: 45 calendar days after submission.
rules.consequence: Late requests are outside the stated window. No penalty on Optum for a slow decision beyond the escalation path; once requested information is supplied, 1703D(a)(3)'s 30-day clock is the statutory argument.
rules.provider_use: Bulk reconsideration letters are expressly allowed, which fits a one-click batch export. Calendar day 45 for a call to Region 2 Provider Services (1-844-839-6108) and then a written overdue notice citing 1703D(a)(3).

rules.citation: Optum Medical Service Model and Claims Guide (Nov. 2026), 'Claim Inquiry / Replacement Claim', p. 2; Optum VA CCN Provider Manual (Nov. 2026), 'Claim Inquiries / Replacement Claims', p. 48 and 'Reimbursement', p. 43
rules.quote: All medical claim inquiries must be submitted within twelve (12) months from the date on the Provider Remittance Advice (PRA) and should include the claim number, date of service, Veteran’s name and justification for the request.
rules.applies_to: Paid VA CCN claims that the practice believes were paid incorrectly (the guide's example: paid amount does not match the fee schedule). The manual calls these inquiries, 'including allowable reviews'.
rules.requires: A written inquiry within 12 months; mail to VA Community Care Network, Attn: Claims, P.O. Box 202118, Florence, SC 29502 (the manual also allows fax). Same 45-day escalation as VA-11. Separately, when VA makes a fee-schedule change retroactive, 'Optum will use the date of service to determine applicable rate and reprocess affected claims at the new published rate.'
rules.deadline: 12 months from the PRA date (manual: 12 months after the claim was initially processed).
rules.consequence: None stated beyond the window.
rules.provider_use: This is the underpayment lane: batch every VA CCN line paid below the practice's contract rate (VA-13) into one inquiry per month, well inside 12 months. Watch VA fee-schedule retroactive revisions and demand reprocessing.

rules.citation: 38 U.S.C. 1703(i)(1); 38 CFR 17.4035 (intro and (a)); VA 'VA fee schedules' page; Optum VA CCN Provider Manual (Nov. 2026), 'Reimbursement', pp. 41-43
rules.quote: The rates paid by VA for hospital care, medical services, or extended care services (hereafter referred to as “services”) furnished pursuant to a procurement contract or an agreement authorized by §§ 17.4100 through 17.4135 will be the rates set forth in the terms of such contract or agreement.
rules.applies_to: VA CCN (contract) and Veterans Care Agreements.
rules.requires: The contract rate governs; under 17.4035(a) rates generally 'will not exceed the applicable Medicare fee schedule ... for the period in which the service was provided' (38 U.S.C. 1703(i)(1) sets the same Medicare ceiling). VA's order: 'Contract-negotiated rate', then the Medicare rate 'including Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) rates', then the VA fee schedule, then a percentage of billed charges. Optum pays the lesser of eligible charges or the contract rate and follows CMS coding rules.
rules.deadline: Disputes go through the 12-month inquiry (VA-12).
rules.consequence: Payment below the contract rate is an underpayment correctable on inquiry.
rules.provider_use: For RemitWatch's 'payer's own rate' check on VA CCN, the expected allowed amount is the practice's Optum/UnitedHealthcare VA CCN payment appendix rate (usually tied to the Medicare/MAC locality rate). The appendix is not public; load it into RemitWatch.

rules.citation: Optum VA CCN Provider Manual (Nov. 2026), 'Other Health Insurance and Veteran Billing' and 'Claim Denials', pp. 45-46; 38 U.S.C. 1703(j)
rules.quote: Veterans are to be held harmless and may not be billed for any reason, including failure to submit claims for reimbursement, failure to submit claims timely, or for claim denials.
rules.applies_to: Every VA CCN service on an approved referral.
rules.requires: 'Providers may not bill Other Health Insurance (OHI) or the Veteran when a Veteran has an approved referral.' 'Payment issued by Optum is considered payment in full for the authorized services.' VA itself recovers from other insurance for non-service-connected care (1703(j): 'the Secretary shall recover or collect reasonable charges ... from a health plan contract').
rules.deadline: None.
rules.consequence: Billing OHI or the Veteran requires a prompt refund and can bring corrective action 'up to and including termination from the network'.
rules.provider_use: Optum is the only collectible source for CCN care, so every CCN dollar must be won from Optum. There is no secondary to bill on CCN claims; RemitWatch should never route a CCN balance to a patient statement or a Medicare/commercial claim, and should flag any OHI payment on a CCN-referred service for refund.

rules.citation: Optum VA CCN Provider Manual (Nov. 2026), 'Covered Services' and 'Request for Services', pp. 9-10
rules.quote: If the services requested are not authorized by VA, the provider may request referral reconsideration from VA. Requests for referral reconsideration must be submitted to VA within ninety (90) days from the date of denial.
rules.applies_to: VA CCN care outside the approved referral or its Standardized Episode of Care (SEOC): for example Mohs repairs, extra stages, pathology or radiation not listed on the SEOC.
rules.requires: 'Any billed CPT codes on a claim which are not listed in the applicable SEOC will result in denial of payment.' The provider must send a Request for Services (VA Form 10-10172) to VA 'the same day the provider determines care is needed', with records and care plan.
rules.deadline: Referral reconsideration to VA within 90 days of VA's denial.
rules.consequence: CPT codes outside the SEOC are denied, and the Veteran cannot be billed.
rules.provider_use: For SEOC denials, the fix runs through VA (RFS or referral reconsideration), then a reconsideration to Optum. RemitWatch should flag billed CPT codes that are not on the referral's SEOC before the claim goes out.

rules.citation: Optum 'Standard Recoupment Process' VA CCN (June 2026); Optum VA CCN Provider Manual (Nov. 2026), 'Claims Audits', p. 49
rules.quote: If the overpayment is not received within sixty-one (61) days from the date of the recoupment letter, the process of offsetting the amount due against future payments to you will begin.
rules.applies_to: Optum recoupments on VA CCN claims.
rules.requires: Letter of intent listing all claims; repayment requested within 30 calendar days; follow-up letter at day 31; offset begins at day 61. Disputes go in writing to VA CCN Correspondence, P.O. Box 202118, Florence, SC (ZIP printed as 29501 here, 29502 elsewhere) with the recoupment letter; medical records are 'neither required nor accepted'; 'Determination timeframe expectation is within thirty (30) business days.' Manual: 'If your reconsideration request is overturned and the offset has already completed, Optum will reimburse the amounts previously recouped.'
rules.deadline: Repay or dispute within 30 calendar days of the letter; offset at day 61; decision expected within 30 business days.
rules.consequence: Offset against future VA CCN payments.
rules.provider_use: Dispute each recoupment within 30 days, cite 1703D(e)(2)-(3) (VA-04), and calendar a check at 30 business days. Track offsets in the payment ledger so a reversed recoupment is reclaimed.

rules.citation: VA Community Care 'Provider claims' page, 'Decision reviews and appeals for Veteran care'
rules.quote: If you provided care under a VA contract, disputes must be submitted in accordance with the terms of your contract.
rules.applies_to: VA CCN claims (the 'contract' is the practice's agreement with Optum/UnitedHealthcare); VCA claims follow the VCA's dispute terms; claims for unauthorized emergency care get Supplemental Claim, Higher-Level Review (both within 1 year of the decision) or a Board appeal.
rules.requires: No separate VA-level appeal of a CCN claim decision was found. VA directs CCN questions to the TPA (Region 2: 844-839-6108) and offers VA Customer Support (877-881-7618) for questions about claims processing or review options.
rules.deadline: Per the provider agreement (not public).
rules.consequence: Escalation beyond Optum's reconsideration runs through the provider agreement's dispute clause.
rules.provider_use: Pull the dispute-resolution clause from the practice's Optum/UHC VA CCN agreement; it defines the next step after reconsideration (possibly arbitration). Use VA Customer Support only for questions or VA-paid claims.

rules.quote: The notice of dispute must be received by the designated VA official to which such notice must be submitted, in accordance with the terms of the Veterans Care Agreement, within 90 calendar days after the accrual of the dispute.
rules.applies_to: Only Veterans Care Agreements (referrals marked 'VCA'); not CCN.
rules.requires: VA decides within 90 calendar days of a complete notice, or up to 150 days with written notice; the decision is the final agency decision; 'An entity or provider must first exhaust the procedures established in this section before seeking judicial review under section 1346 of title 28 U.S.C.' Accrual for underpayment or denial = the date the payment or denial notice was received.
rules.deadline: 90 calendar days from receipt of the payment or denial notice; VA decision in 90 (max 150) days.
rules.consequence: Missing the 90 days loses the exclusive administrative remedy; a timely dispute gives a VA decision deadline and a path to federal court.
rules.provider_use: If any VA claims run under a VCA, this is the strongest VA route: a fixed VA decision deadline plus court review after exhaustion.

rules.citation: 38 CFR 17.276(a)-(b), (d); VA 'Decision reviews and appeals - Family member care' and 'CHAMPVA' pages; VA Financial Policy Vol. VIII ch. 02 sec. 020507
rules.quote: CHAMPVA is the last payer to OHI, as that term is defined in § 17.270(b). CHAMPVA benefits will generally not be paid until the claim has been filed with the OHI and the OHI has issued a final payment determination or explanation of benefits. CHAMPVA is secondary payer to Medicare per the terms of § 17.271(b).
rules.applies_to: CHAMPVA (spouses, children and survivors of eligible Veterans), usually secondary to Medicare. VA, not Optum, pays (medical payer ID 84146).
rules.requires: Claims filed within one year of the date of service (exceptions for good cause, including delay by the primary insurer). Provider reviews: Higher-Level Review 'within 1 year of the decision'; Supplemental Claim 'may be submitted anytime'; Board appeal.
rules.deadline: 1 year from date of service; Higher-Level Review 1 year from the decision.
rules.consequence: Late claims denied unless an exception is granted. VA's financial policy lists CHAMPVA claims as exempt from the Prompt Payment Act.
rules.provider_use: Put CHAMPVA balances left after Medicare into the 'secondary never billed' sweep. Do not claim Prompt Payment Act interest on CHAMPVA.

rules.quote: The additional penalty shall be equal to one hundred (100) percent of the original late payment interest penalty but must not exceed $5,000.
rules.applies_to: Federal agency payments to vendors under procurement contracts. For community care VA says it follows 1703D (VA-06), and 1703D only borrows the PPA rate. Not confirmed to apply to Optum-paid CCN claims; CHAMPVA is exempt per VA policy; arguable for VA-paid VCA claims (sec. 020507 lists VCAs as PPA-subject).
rules.requires: Interest from the day after the due date to payment; interest of $1.00 or more paid without request, with a notice of amount, rate and period (3902(c)(1)-(2)); additional penalty when interest is not paid within 10 days after payment and the vendor demands it in writing by day 40 after payment (minimum $25, maximum $5,000, per invoice, 5 CFR 1315.11); unpaid interest compounds every 30 days (3902(e)); interest stops after one year (3907(b)(1)(B)); none while a dispute over the amount is pending (3907(c)).
rules.deadline: Additional-penalty demand: postmarked, faxed or emailed by the 40th day after payment.
rules.consequence: Additional penalty of 100% of the missed interest (min $25, max $5,000) where the Act applies.
rules.provider_use: Use the 40-day additional-penalty demand only where VA itself pays under an arrangement VA treats as PPA-subject (for example a VCA), after confirming. Do not assert it against Optum on CCN claims.

rules.citation: VA Community Care 'Debt collection' page (for VA-paid claims)
rules.quote: From the date of the BOC/NOI, you have 30 days to: submit payment, or request review, or submit documentation showing proof of prior repayment.
rules.applies_to: Overpayments VA itself paid (VCA, CHAMPVA, other VA-direct claims); not Optum CCN recoupments (VA-16).
rules.requires: VA issues a Bill of Collection and Notice of Indebtedness; after 30 days VA may offset future VA payments and assess fees; after 120 days VA may refer the debt to the Treasury Offset Program.
rules.deadline: 30 days from the BOC/NOI date to request review.
rules.consequence: Offset of future VA payments; Treasury offset after 120 days.
rules.provider_use: Request review within 30 days of every VA Notice of Indebtedness, citing 1703D(e).

rules.quote: Sections 3729 through 3733 of title 31 shall apply to fraudulent claims for payment submitted to the Secretary by a health care entity or provider under this chapter.
rules.applies_to: The practice: every claim and claim-related statement to VA or its contractor.
rules.requires: The False Claims Act applies to VA community care claims, and VA 'shall bar' a provider it determines submitted fraudulent claims (1703D(c)(2)). 'Fraudulent claims' means knowing misrepresentation of a material fact to induce payment (1703D(i)(4)).
rules.deadline: None.
rules.consequence: False Claims Act liability and exclusion from VA community care.
rules.provider_use: This is a constraint on the letters, not leverage: every fact, date and dollar figure in an automated VA or TRICARE letter must be exact, and claims of legal entitlement must match the text (for example, interest under 1703D is 'may', not 'shall').

rules.quote: 95 percent of all clean claims must be processed not later than 30 days after the date that such claims are submitted to the claims processor; and (B) 100 percent of all clean claims must be processed not later than 100 days after the date that such claims are submitted to the claims processor.
rules.applies_to: All TRICARE claims: TRICARE East (Humana Military, claims processed by PGBA), which covers Kentucky and Indiana, and TRICARE For Life (WPS). Network and non-network providers.
rules.requires: DoD must run a claims system meeting both standards. Clean claim: 'a claim that has no defect, impropriety (including a lack of any required substantiating documentation), or particular circumstance requiring special treatment that prevents timely payment'.
rules.deadline: 30 days (95% of clean claims) and 100 days (all clean claims) from submission.
rules.consequence: No penalty stated; a clean claim unprocessed at day 100 is outside the statutory standard.
rules.provider_use: Age TRICARE claims from the 277CA date. After day 30, a status request citing 1095c(a)(1)(A); at day 100, a written demand stating the claim is outside the 100-percent standard of 1095c(a)(1)(B).

rules.quote: The Secretary may, under the system required by paragraph (1) and consistent with the provisions in chapter 39 of title 31 (commonly referred to as the “Prompt Payment Act”), require that interest be paid on clean claims that are not processed within 30 days.
rules.applies_to: TRICARE clean claims not processed within 30 days.
rules.requires: Discretionary interest. Whether the TRICARE Operations Manual (6010.62-M) requires contractors to pay it could not be confirmed: manuals.health.mil was unreachable from this environment (certificate failure, then HTTP 503).
rules.deadline: Day 31 after submission, if interest applies.
rules.consequence: Not confirmed.
rules.provider_use: Request interest at the Treasury rate on clean TRICARE claims paid after day 30, citing 1095c(a)(2), and ask the contractor to state its interest policy in writing.

rules.quote: shall limit the information required in support of claims for payment for health care items and services provided under the TRICARE program to that information that is identical to the information that would be required for claims for reimbursement for those items and services under title XVIII of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395 et seq.) except for that information, if any, that is uniquely required by the TRICARE program.
rules.applies_to: TRICARE claims.
rules.requires: TRICARE may not demand more claim information than Medicare would, other than information uniquely required by TRICARE.
rules.deadline: None.
rules.consequence: A denial or pend for information Medicare would not require is open to challenge.
rules.provider_use: Answer 'requested information not received' denials and records demands by citing 1095c(d) where Medicare would pay the same code without that documentation.

rules.quote: all claims submitted for benefits must, except as provided in paragraph (d)(2) of this section, be filed with the appropriate CHAMPUS contractor no later than one year after the services are provided. Unless the requirement is waived, failure to file a claim within this deadline waives all rights to benefits for such services or supplies.
rules.applies_to: All TRICARE claims, including TRICARE For Life. Humana Military separately asks network providers to file electronically 'within 90 days of the date care was provided' (a contract expectation, not the regulatory deadline).
rules.requires: File within one year of service. A returned claim must be resubmitted by the later of one year after the service or '90 days from the date the claim was returned'. Exceptions include '(B) Administrative error ... of an officer or employee of OCHAMPUS ... or a CHAMPUS fiscal intermediary' and '(D) Delays by other health insurance' when coordination is required.
rules.deadline: One year from the date of service; returned claims: later of one year or 90 days from return.
rules.consequence: Late filing 'waives all rights to benefits'.
rules.provider_use: Hard stop at one year for TRICARE and TFL secondaries; when a contractor's error or the primary payer's delay caused the miss, request an exception under 199.7(d)(2)(i)(B) or (D) with documentation.

rules.quote: OCHAMPUSEUR, the CHAMPUS contractor, or CHAMPUS peer review organization normally shall issue its reconsideration determination no later than 60 days from the date of receipt of the request for reconsideration
rules.applies_to: Appealable TRICARE determinations, for appropriate appealing parties (beneficiaries, participating providers, or a network provider appointed by the beneficiary).
rules.requires: Reconsideration 'must be mailed within 90 days after the date of the notice of initial determination'; contractor 'normally' decides within 60 days. Formal review by DHA: request within 60 days; decided 'normally' within 90 days; available if the amount in dispute is $50 or more. Hearing: amount in dispute $300 or more, request within 60 days. Claims for the same beneficiary and same issue can be combined to reach these amounts once one has been reconsidered. A request with too small an amount in dispute 'may not be rejected at the reconsideration level of appeal.'
rules.deadline: Reconsideration request 90 days; contractor decision normally 60 days; formal review request 60 days; DHA decision normally 90 days; hearing request 60 days.
rules.consequence: Reconsideration is final if the amount in dispute is under $50 or no formal review is requested in 60 days.
rules.provider_use: Small-dollar items still get reconsideration on the merits. Track the 60-day decision norm and escalate to formal review where the combined same-patient, same-issue amount reaches $50 (hearing at $300).

rules.quote: A nonparticipating provider is not a party to the initial determination and may not appeal.
rules.applies_to: TRICARE appeals.
rules.requires: Not appealable: '(ii) The amount of the CHAMPUS-determined allowable cost or charge, since the methodology for determining allowable costs or charges is established by this part.' For Medicare-eligible (TFL) patients, a Medicare denial for a patient-specific reason is appealed through Medicare; a TRICARE denial after Medicare paid carries normal TRICARE appeal rights.
rules.deadline: As in TR-05.
rules.consequence: Formal appeals are unavailable for allowable-amount disputes and for nonparticipating providers.
rules.provider_use: Route allowable-amount and contract-rate disputes to the contractor's administrative/allowable charge review (TR-07), not appeals; route Medicare-denied TFL lines through Medicare appeals.

rules.citation: Humana Military, TRICARE Provider Handbook, East Region 2026, 'Claims adjustments and allowable charge reviews' and 'Administrative reviews', p. 67
rules.quote: Administrative reviews must be postmarked or received within 90 calendar days of the date of beneficiary’s EOB or the provider remittance.
rules.applies_to: TRICARE East (Kentucky and Indiana) network and non-network providers. Reviewable issues include allowable charge complaints, duplicate and 'included in a paid service' denials, claims auditing denials, 'requested information was not received', late filing, lack of authorization, coding, cost-share, eligibility, keying errors, 'Network provider disputes relating to contractual reimbursement amount', OHI and wrong procedure code.
rules.requires: Written request stating the reason, with the claim, EOB or remittance, and supporting records. Administrative reviews: TRICARE East Region claims department, PO Box 202147, Florence, SC 29502-2147. Allowable charge reviews: Humana Military, ATTN: Allowable charge review, PO Box 202146, Florence, SC 29502-2146, fax (877) 489-0011.
rules.deadline: 90 calendar days from the EOB or remittance date.
rules.consequence: Outside 90 days the review is not timely. The handbook states no response deadline for Humana Military.
rules.provider_use: This is the TRICARE lane for underpayments against the network contract rate and for most denials. Batch by remittance date so each review lands well inside 90 days.

rules.citation: Humana Military, TRICARE Provider Handbook, East Region 2026, 'Appealing a decision' p. 53 and 'Claim appeals' p. 68
rules.quote: Network providers are not a proper appealing party, but can appeal on behalf of the beneficiary with a signed Appointment of representation form from the beneficiary.
rules.applies_to: TRICARE East denials for medical necessity or coverage (factual determinations); proper appealing parties include beneficiaries and 'Participating non-network TRICARE-authorized providers'.
rules.requires: 'Appeal requests must be postmarked or received within 90 calendar days of the date of the denial.' Non-appealable items (allowed amounts, coding, timely filing, OHI, network provider/contractor disputes) go to administrative review. Fax (877) 850-1046; Humana Military Appeals, PO Box 740044, Louisville, KY 40201-7444.
rules.deadline: 90 calendar days from the denial.
rules.consequence: Network providers must hold beneficiaries harmless for noncovered care unless the beneficiary signed a waiver.
rules.provider_use: If the practice is in Humana Military's network, get a signed Appointment of Representative at intake for TRICARE patients so medical-necessity denials can be appealed without chasing a signature later.

rules.citation: Humana Military, TRICARE Provider Handbook, East Region 2026, 'TRICARE For Life (TFL)' and 'How TFL works', pp. 25-26; tricare.mil 'Regions' page; tricare.mil 'Filing Claims' page
rules.quote: File TFL claims first with Medicare. Medicare pays its portion and electronically forwards the claim to TRICARE Medicare Eligible Program (TMEP), (unless the beneficiary has OHI). TMEP sends its payment for TRICARE-covered services directly to the provider.
rules.applies_to: Military retirees and family members with Medicare Part A and B (TRICARE For Life), the TRICARE group most likely in a Medicare-heavy dermatology practice. tricare.mil lists 'WPS Government Services' as the TFL partner; TMEP phone (866) 773-0404.
rules.requires: Crossover from Medicare should be automatic; TFL pays after Medicare for services both cover. tricare.mil: 'In the U.S. and U.S. territories, you must file your claims within one year of service.'
rules.deadline: One year from the date of service (32 CFR 199.7(d)).
rules.consequence: A failed crossover leaves the TFL share unpaid unless the practice files it within the year.
rules.provider_use: Sweep Medicare remittances for TFL patients whose secondary never posted and file those with TMEP inside the one-year window; these are often the small balances the owner wants chased.

rules.citation: Humana Military, TRICARE Provider Handbook, East Region 2026, pp. 8, 54, 65, 69-70
rules.quote: Please wait at least 45 days after submitting a claim before contacting Humana Military.
rules.applies_to: TRICARE East providers (the handbook lists Indiana and Kentucky in the East Region; 'PGBA, LLC (PGBA) is the Humana Military partner for claims processing in the TRICARE East Region'; payer ID 99727).
rules.requires: Network providers accept the contract rate as payment for covered services and must hold beneficiaries harmless for noncovered care; 'Providers are not permitted to bill TRICARE beneficiaries for services rejected by claims auditing'; non-network non-participating providers 'may only bill the beneficiary up to 115 percent of the TRICARE-allowable charge'.
rules.deadline: 45 days after submission before a status call (handbook expectation).
rules.consequence: Improper beneficiary billing can affect TRICARE and Medicare status.
rules.provider_use: Start TRICARE status follow-up at day 45, written demand at day 100 (TR-01). Never shift claims-auditing denials to the patient.

batch_and_channel: Optum VA CCN (Region 2: Kentucky and Indiana): reconsiderations may list multiple claims in a single letter (manual p. 48). Send to the address or fax printed on the remittance advice; otherwise secure fax 1-877-666-6597, secure email faxAG2@optumserve.com, or mail to VA Community Care Network, Appeals and Grievance Team MS-21, 3237 Airport Road, La Crosse, WI 54603 (the claims guide prints 56403, likely a typo).

Optum underpayment (claim inquiry, 'allowable review'): within 12 months of the PRA date, by mail to VA Community Care Network, Attn: Claims, P.O. Box 202118, Florence, SC 29502 (the manual also allows fax). Group lines into one inquiry per month by PRA date.

Optum escalation: no answer 45 calendar days after a reconsideration or inquiry -> call CCN Provider Services Region 2, 1-844-839-6108 (8 a.m.-6 p.m. local, Mon-Fri), then send a written overdue notice citing 38 U.S.C. 1703D(a)(3) and (d)(1).

Optum recoupment disputes: in writing to VA CCN Correspondence, P.O. Box 202118, Florence, SC (29501 on the recoupment sheet, 29502 elsewhere), with the recoupment letter; file within 30 days of the letter so the dispute precedes the day-61 offset; no medical records.
Optum electronic claims: payer ID VACCN; remittances arrive as 835s. Use the 277CA acceptance date as proof of receipt for the 30-day 1703D clock and the 180-day filing rule.

VA direct (VCA, CHAMPVA, unauthorized emergency): VA medical payer ID 12115; CHAMPVA medical 84146. Family-member reviews go to VFMP Appeals, PO Box 600, Spring City, PA 19475 (Higher-Level Review within 1 year; Supplemental Claim any time). VA Customer Support 877-881-7618.
VA Veterans Care Agreements only: written notice of dispute to the VA official named in the VCA within 90 days of the payment or denial notice; VA must decide within 90 days (150 with notice).

TRICARE East (Humana Military/PGBA): payer ID 99727. Administrative reviews to TRICARE East Region claims department, PO Box 202147, Florence, SC 29502-2147. Allowable charge reviews to Humana Military, ATTN: Allowable charge review, PO Box 202146, Florence, SC 29502-2146, fax (877) 489-0011. Medical-necessity appeals by fax (877) 850-1046 or Humana Military Appeals, PO Box 740044, Louisville, KY 40201-7444. All within 90 days of the EOB/remittance or denial.

TRICARE small claims: 32 CFR 199.10 says a request with too small an amount in dispute 'may not be rejected at the reconsideration level'. Same-beneficiary, same-issue claims can be combined to reach $50 (formal review) or $300 (hearing) once one has been reconsidered.
TRICARE For Life: Medicare crosses over to TMEP (WPS) automatically; TMEP (866) 773-0404. Chase missing secondaries inside 1 year from the date of service.

Cadence that fits the rules: VA CCN unanswered at day 31 after acceptance -> overdue letter; day 45 after any Optum submission -> phone escalation; day 150 -> last resubmission window before the 180-day filing limit. TRICARE: status at day 45, demand at day 100, appeal/review inside 90 days of each remittance.
does_not_apply: Kentucky and Indiana prompt-pay statutes and the state insurance departments: no primary source was found applying them to VA CCN (a federal program paid under a VA contract) or to TRICARE. Humana Military's handbook states that 'Unless specified otherwise, federal laws generally supersede state laws.' Treat state prompt-pay interest as not available for VA and TRICARE claims unless counsel confirms otherwise.
ERISA and the self-funded vs fully-insured distinction: not the framework here. VA CCN, CHAMPVA and TRICARE are federal government programs, not employer plans.
Automatic interest: 38 U.S.C. 1703D(d)(2) and 10 U.S.C. 1095c(a)(2) both say the Secretary 'may' require interest. Neither creates an automatic interest right or a penalty.
Prompt Payment Act additional penalty (5 CFR 1315.11): written for agency payments to vendors; not confirmed for Optum-paid CCN claims; CHAMPVA is listed as PPA-exempt in VA's financial policy.

Billing the Veteran or other insurance for CCN-referred care: prohibited (hold harmless; Optum payment is payment in full; VA itself recovers from other insurance under 38 U.S.C. 1703(j)). CCN claims have no secondary payer for the practice.
Timely-filing waivers from Optum: the claims guide says Optum is 'contractually prohibited' from waiving timely filing except for claims first misdirected to VA or another VA TPA.
The Veterans Care Agreement dispute process (38 CFR 17.4135) and its court path do not apply to CCN claims.
38 CFR 17.132, 17.133 and 17.277 (reconsideration within 1 year) apply only to 'legacy claims', not current ones.

TRICARE formal appeals: not available to nonparticipating providers (32 CFR 199.10(a)(2)(i)(E)), not for the allowable-charge amount (199.10(a)(6)(ii)), and not to network providers unless appointed by the beneficiary (Humana handbook). Those disputes go to administrative/allowable charge review.
TRICARE For Life lines Medicare denied for a patient-specific reason: appealed through Medicare, not TRICARE (32 CFR 199.10(a)(1)(ii)(B)(1)).
open_questions: Does Optum pay interest on CCN clean claims paid after 30 days? Not stated in the November 2026 manual; VA's financial policy is internally inconsistent. Ask Optum in writing and check the practice's VA CCN payment appendix.

The practice's Optum/UnitedHealthcare VA CCN participation agreement and payment appendix (dispute-resolution or arbitration clause, refund deadlines, rates) are not public and were not reviewed; they control escalation after reconsideration and the expected allowed amount for underpayment checks.
VA's 1703D(f) clean-claim list: VA requested comments in 2019 (84 FR 32670); no final published list was found.

TRICARE Operations Manual 6010.62-M (claims timeliness and interest): manuals.health.mil was unreachable (certificate failure, then HTTP 503), so any contractor interest obligation there is unconfirmed.
Humana Military's network agreement terms on payment timing or interest are not public.

Optum's own documents conflict on details: the reconsideration clock starts at the 'date of denial' (manual) or the PRA date (guide); the late-referral filing clock runs from Optum's receipt of the referral (manual) or VA's issuance (guide); the La Crosse ZIP is 54603 vs 56403; Florence is 29501 vs 29502. Use the earlier date and the manual's address until Optum confirms.
Whether 1703D's 30/45-day standard reaches CHAMPVA claims: CHAMPVA is under 38 U.S.C. chapter 17, but VA treats CHAMPVA under its own 1-year rule and lists it as PPA-exempt. Unconfirmed.
Whether Optum recoupments are 'deductions' covered by 1703D(e)'s notice-and-decide-first protections is not confirmed.
The Prompt Payment rate for January-June 2027 was not yet published as of 2026-11-23.
VA's annual 1703D(d)(3) reports to Congress on overdue claims were not located; they could show Optum Region 2 late-payment rates useful in letters.
